description: Mechanic-aware authored world construction, narrative semantics, design-system planning, and progression-facing world identity extracted from the clone world-design stage.

skills.title: Map mechanics into themed world semantics
skills.intent: Translate avatar, hazards, rewards, goals, score, and failure semantics into the remix world without changing the underlying mechanics.
required_actions: Map player, hazards, collectibles, goals, timers, and failure states into world-specific meanings.
Label each mapping with why it is safe or where runtime verification is needed.
Keep the mappings cosmetic, copy-facing, or media-facing rather than logic-changing.
acceptance_bar: Every semantic reframe corresponds to a real gameplay surface.
The world mapping preserves mechanic truth.

skills.title: Unify HUD vocabulary and gameplay-facing tone
skills.intent: Keep terminology, instructions, progress cues, and narrative framing coherent across screens.
required_actions: Choose stable terms for the same gameplay concepts.
Keep gameplay-facing copy short, actionable, and truthful.
Let the world framing support readability rather than obscure mechanics.
acceptance_bar: The player-facing loop reads as one consistent fantasy.
HUD labels remain understandable on mobile.
failure_modes_prevented: Copy that hides the real goal

skills.title: Define an authored world, not just labels
skills.intent: Give the remix a recognizable setting, tone, reward fantasy, failure fantasy, and visual motif set that can drive later implementation.
required_actions: Define setting, tone, player role, pressure source, reward fantasy, failure fantasy, and key nouns.
Ensure the world supports animation, procedural art, and progression.
Keep the world specific enough that later stages do not have to improvise identity.
acceptance_bar: The remixed world is immediately recognizable and coherent.
Visual and QA phases can execute against a stable authored-world target.
failure_modes_prevented: No narrative frame for visual execution

skills.title: Express progression as distinct but related worlds
skills.intent: Carry the five-level plan into world identity, background evolution, and metaverse-style continuity.
required_actions: Assign level names, world beats, background evolution, and character/item/prop additions for each progression stage.
Keep continuity through shared motifs, UI language, and core play identity.
Differentiate worlds through controlled scene, palette, atmosphere, and storytelling changes.
acceptance_bar: Progression feels like one game family moving through staged worlds.
Later levels are not random reskins.
failure_modes_prevented: Five levels with no world identity

skills.title: Reject weak stock-scene ownership
skills.intent: Force the authored world to replace or demote boring static stock backgrounds as the dominant playfield identity.
required_actions: Inspect whether a static image currently owns the scene.
Mark weak generic backgrounds as non-protected.
Define a procedural replacement background with motion, semantic motifs, and level/state reactivity.
acceptance_bar: The intended world is the real scene foundation, not garnish around a stock image.
failure_modes_prevented: Wrapper polish around an unchanged stock scene
Background identity detached from the remix premise
Decorative layers obscuring the real need for authored scenery

skills.title: Write a role-based `remix_theme.json`
skills.intent: Define the design system as implementation guidance rather than a loose mood board.
required_actions: Define palette roles, shape language, typography tone, CTA treatment, hazard/reward differentiation, and background cues.
Express mapping from current/default treatments into remix-specific roles.
Keep the artifact compact but concrete enough for later phases to execute directly.
acceptance_bar: Visual phases can restyle the game consistently from this artifact.
The theme system reinforces readability and the authored world.
failure_modes_prevented: World identity not propagating into UI and scene work

skills.title: Define the procedural motif language
skills.intent: Specify how player, enemies, props, collectibles, particles, and background motifs should belong to one reusable visual family.
required_actions: Define silhouettes, motifs, animation rules, and icon logic for major world elements.
Prefer CSS, SVG, Canvas, DOM shapes, and lightweight generated components.
Ensure recognizability survives even if stock images disappear.
acceptance_bar: The remix has a recognizable motif system.
World, entities, and UI can all derive from the same visual grammar.
failure_modes_prevented: Remix identity depending entirely on pasted art
